comparisons.peer_topic: Intel 4 process node production status and capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel 4, the first EUV lithography node, delivered significant density scaling and approximately 20% performance-per-watt improvement over Intel 7; it moved to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland in 2024 for the Intel Core Ultra processor and is expected to represent an increasing portion of production in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight specific manufacturing process nodes and their technological advancements in 2024. Micron reports volume production of HBM3E enabled by its advanced 1β process node, focusing on increased bandwidth and power efficiency. Similarly, Intel identifies Intel 4 as its first EUV lithography node which delivered significant density scaling and performance-per-watt improvements over its previous node (Intel 7), moving to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland. Both disclosures detail the progression from previous generation architectures to newer nodes that offer enhanced physical and electrical characteristics for AI and high-performance computing workloads.

sentences.text: In 2024, we began volume production of our 8-high 24GB HBM3E with increased bandwidth and superior power efficiency enabled by our advanced 1β process node.

▪Intel 4, our first EUV lithography node, delivers significant density scaling and approximately 20% performance-per-watt improvement over Intel 7. The Intel Core Ultra processor is our first high-volume client product on Intel 4 and began shipping to customers in 2023. Intel 4 moved to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland in 2024, and is expected to represent an increasing portion of our processor production and products in 2025.

comparisons.peer_topic: NVIDIA RTX Technology and AI Integration
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA RTX enhances gaming through real-time ray tracing for cinematic-quality rendering and DLSS, an AI technology that boosts frame rates, positioning RTX as the AI PC leader with over 100 million AI-capable PCs and 500+ enabled applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures describe the integration of AI capabilities into their respective product lines in 2024. Micron’s disclosure focuses on the hardware level, stating it began volume production of HBM3E with 'superior power efficiency' and started shipments of HBM3E 12-high units to 'enable qualifications across the AI ecosystem.' NVIDIA’s disclosure describes its RTX technology as bringing 'next generation graphics and AI to games' via DLSS, an 'AI technology that boosts frame rates,' and positions itself as the 'AI PC leader' with over 100 million AI-capable PCs. While Micron supplies the underlying memory component essential for AI training and inference, NVIDIA emphasizes the software/hardware stack that enables AI-driven performance enhancements for end-users.

sentences.text: In 2024, we began volume production of our 8-high 24GB HBM3E with increased bandwidth and superior power efficiency enabled by our advanced 1β process node.
We have also started shipments of production-capable HBM3E 12-high 36GB units to enable qualifications across the AI ecosystem.
We developed NVIDIA RTX to bring next generation graphics and AI to games.
NVIDIA RTX also features deep learning super sampling, or NVIDIA DLSS, our AI technology that boosts frame rates while generating beautiful, sharp images for games.
With an installed base of over 100 million AI capable PCs, more than 500 RTX AI-enabled applications and games, and a robust suite of development tools, RTX is already the AI PC leader.
